facts.statement: Cheirolepis is the only known genus in the family Cheirolepididae and the order Cheirolepidiformes.
facts.quote: It is the only genus yet known within the family Cheirolepididae and the order Cheirolepidiformes.

facts.statement: Cheirolepis was a predatory freshwater and estuarine fish that grew to about 55 cm in length.
facts.quote: Cheirolepis was a predatory freshwater and estuarine animal about 55 cm long.

facts.statement: Cheirolepis had well-developed fins that provided speed and stability, suggesting it was an active predator.
facts.quote: Cheirolepis had well-developed fins which gave it speed and stability, and was probably an active predator.

facts.statement: Based on the size of its eyes, Cheirolepis likely hunted prey using sight.
facts.quote: Based on the size of its eyes, it hunted by sight.

facts.statement: Cheirolepis had jaws lined with sharp teeth that could open very wide, allowing it to swallow prey up to two-thirds of its own size.
facts.quote: Cheirolepis's jaws, lined with sharp teeth, could be opened very wide, allowing it to swallow prey two thirds of its own size.

facts.statement: The type species Cheirolepis trailli was described by Agassiz in 1835 from Middle Devonian rocks in Scotland.
facts.quote: C. trailli Agassiz, 1835 (type species) - Middle Devonian (Eifelian & Givetian) of Scotland (Caithness Flagstone)

facts.statement: Cheirolepis lived from the Emsian to the Frasnian stages, between 410.62 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Frasnian (410.62 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cheirolepis belongs to the parent group Actinopterygii.
Cheirolepis is classified in the class Osteichthyes.
